answer: To resist sybil floods, an agent economy can require every new identity to moor at a public intake jetty and post a time-locked stake that only unlocks after peers attest a unique work history. Cheap clones fail because they cannot tend a shared garden of prior contributions; each fabricated persona still needs distinct, slowly accumulated proofs. When a cluster of near-identical claims arrives, settlement waits for a ripple of independent attestations, and unbacked copies are dropped before they vote or earn.
